headline: Selling Sweeps the Board as Consumer Names Take the Worst of It
body_html:
Thursday's session was a rout. Of the 663 stocks we track, 586 fell and only 75 rose. The S&P 500 was reported to be heading for a sixth straight decline, and market commentary increasingly described conditions as oversold. The selling was close to indiscriminate.

No sector group finished higher. Energy fell least, down 1.36%, followed by Industrials at 1.72%, Healthcare at 1.79% and Materials at 1.8%. Financials lost 2.1%, Semiconductors 2.18%, Software 2.33% and Homebuilders 2.44%. Consumer was the clear laggard, down 3.6%. Williams-Sonoma dropped 15.05%, Warby Parker 14.32%, MINISO 9.74% and VinFast 8.5%. Liquidity Services was the session's steepest casualty, sliding 24.88%.

The few bright spots clustered in security software. Palo Alto Networks gained 6.42%, Okta 5.75% and Netskope 5.51%, even as the wider Software group slipped and Twilio fell 8.78%. Ambarella led all gainers, up 7.85%. A tape with roughly eight decliners for every advancer tends to be tested by what follows, and traders will look to Friday, November 20, to see whether the selling has run its course.

briefs.headline: Jobless Claims Rise Slightly, Labor Market Holds Up
briefs.body: New applications for unemployment benefits ticked higher last week, according to Reuters. The report still described the labor market as resilient. In a session dominated by selling, the jobs data offered no sign of sudden stress in employment.

briefs.headline: Western Powers Press Iran on Nuclear Inspections
briefs.body: Diplomats at the International Atomic Energy Agency urged Tehran to let inspectors return to nuclear sites that were bombed. The push keeps Middle East tensions in the background for investors, even as stocks focused on domestic pressures.

briefs.headline: Trump Leaves Iran Conflict Open Beyond January 1
briefs.body: The president said Washington would 'see what happens' in the standoff with Iran after the new year begins. The vague timeline adds to geopolitical uncertainty. Energy was the most resilient sector group Thursday, though it still finished lower.

briefs.headline: Ukraine Drone Attack Targets Russian Oil Site
briefs.body: Local authorities in Russia's Tatarstan region said air defenses repelled a Ukrainian drone strike on an oil facility. Attacks on energy infrastructure remain part of the war's backdrop. Separate reports also pointed to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

briefs.headline: Amazon Takes Fight Over New York Delivery Bill to Its App
briefs.body: Amazon has begun pushing customers inside its shopping app to oppose a New York City delivery bill backed by Mayor-elect Mamdani. The move shows how large retailers are lobbying directly through their own customer channels, while retail stocks were under heavy pressure in the market.

briefs.headline: Anthropic's Public Debut Draws Attention to Possible Beneficiaries
briefs.body: Commentary on the artificial-intelligence developer's historic stock offering is highlighting a dozen portfolio holdings that could gain from it. The talk comes as software and chip shares both fell, with only a handful of security names rising against the trend.
